question.problem: If $[a]_{n}$ denotes the residue class containing all integers congruent to $a$ modulo $n,$ then $[-26]_{6}=$
question.worked_solution:
We have $[a]_{6}=[b]_{6}$ if 

$$
a≡b\,(\text{mod}\,6).
$$

The residue class $[-26]_{6}$ consists of the elements that are congruent to $-26$ modulo $6.$ 

We can find an alternative representation for this residue class as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[-26]_{6} & ={x\in Z\,|\,x≡-26\,(\text{mod}\,6)} \\  & ={x\in Z\,|\,x≡(-5)\cdot 6+4\,(\text{mod}\,6)} \\  & ={x\in Z\,|\,x≡(-5)\cdot 0+4\,(\text{mod}\,6)} \\  & ={x\in Z\,|\,x≡4\,(\text{mod}\,6)} \\  & =[4]_{6}\end{aligned}
$$
